verdict.rationale: LangSmith's docs say you can build datasets from historical production traces, including adding real failing traces as test cases. They also document running the application against those datasets as experiments, scored by human, code, LLM-as-judge, or pairwise evaluators, to compare versions and catch regressions. missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of the trace-to-dataset and offline experiment workflow.

support.subject: As an ML engineer, I can curate datasets from production traces and run offline evaluations against them

citations.quote: Create a dataset with examples from manually curated test cases, historical production traces, or synthetic data generation.
Add real traces to a dataset so a failure you saw once becomes a test you run every time.
Execute your application on the dataset to create an experiment. Configure repetitions, concurrency, and caching to optimize runs.
Run evaluations on curated datasets during development to compare versions, benchmark performance, and catch regressions.
Create evaluators to score performance: Human review, Code rules, LLM-as-judge, Pairwise comparison
